podcast.title: Extremely Upfront and Suggestive About Sex
podcast.body: Carol Pope was "extremely up front and extremely suggestive when it came to sex," challenging societal norms and making bold statements through her music and persona. She was a woman openly declaring her lesbian identity in the early 1980s rock scene, which was almost unprecedented at the time. "Here was a woman being totally up front about being a lesbian. Who was doing that in the early 80s in the world of rock? Pretty much no one."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Early Days of LGBTQ Rock

podcast.title: First Openly Gay Alt-Rock Role Model (Canadian)
podcast.body: Carol Pope is identified as one of the first openly gay alt-rock role models in the world, and notably, she was Canadian. She fronted the Toronto group Rough Trade. "One of the first openly gay, alt-rock role models in the world was a woman and a Canadian."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Early Days of LGBTQ Rock

podcast.title: Rough Trade Band Name Origin
podcast.body: The name of her band, Rough Trade, was itself a term derived from gay subculture, directly signaling their connection to the community. "Carol Pope fronted rough trade, a Toronto group whose very name was a term from gay subculture."
